transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um... I hope I explain this right. I guess I came in because... well, I've been having this really heavy feeling lately. I don't want to sound dramatic or complain too much, but it just feels kind of hopeless right now. 

Like... after my divorce, I worked so hard to build everything back up, and now it just feels like it's all collapsed again, and I'm just sort of sitting underneath it. I'm sorry, I know I should be handling things better, but... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking?
Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

Um... I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I mean, everyone has bad days, right? I usually try really hard to just push through and, you know, focus on my work and stay positive. I really don't like being a downer. 

So... I don't think I've ever felt quite *this* stuck before. Or maybe I just didn't let myself realize it? I've always tried to just keep everything together so I wouldn't be a burden to anyone. I'm sorry, I know that's probably not a very helpful answer. Is it okay if I'm not completely sure?
Since you've been feeling this way, have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns, such as trouble falling asleep or waking up much earlier than you intend to?

Um... well, I guess my sleep hasn't been the greatest lately. I mean, I really try to get a full eight hours, because I know how important that is, but... it's just been a little tricky. 

Sometimes I just lie there staring at the ceiling, and my brain just won't turn off. I just keep replaying, you know, bills I need to pay or little mistakes I made at work. I know I shouldn't dwell on those things, I really try not to. And then other times, I'll wake up way before dawn, and it just feels like I didn't actually sleep at all. 

I'm probably just letting the stress get to me too much. I know a lot of people have trouble sleeping, so I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. Does that sound like the kind of thing you're asking about? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Can you tell me exactly when you started feeling this way in relation to a specific event or change in your life?

Um... I think it's been about a month now? I hope that's specific enough. 

It kind of started around the time I was trying to sort out all the financial stuff after the divorce. It got a little messy, and I think I just let it overwhelm me more than I should have. I know I should be better at managing stress, especially with my job, but... yeah, it's just been hanging over me since then. 

I really tried to just push through it and not let it affect my work or anything. I don't want to sound like I'm just making excuses, but... is a month a normal amount of time to feel this way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
Beyond the feelings of sadness and hopelessness you described, have you also been feeling particularly anxious, nervous, or on edge lately?

Um... I wouldn't say I've been super anxious, really. I mean, I guess I get a little nervous sometimes, but isn't that normal when you're going through a lot? 

I really try to keep things in perspective and not let myself get too worked up. I don't want to be one of those people who's always panicking over every little thing, you know? I try to stay calm, especially at work, because people depend on me. 

So... maybe a little on edge sometimes, just with everything going on, but I don't think it's anything out of the ordinary. I hope that's okay to say? I just don't want to exaggerate and make it seem like I'm a nervous wreck or anything. Is that the kind of anxiety you mean?

When you say you feel 'a little on edge,' does that feeling ever reach a point where it interferes with your ability to get through your daily responsibilities or makes it difficult for you to concentrate on your work?

Um... well, I guess it has been a little harder to focus lately, but I really try not to let it show at work. I mean, I know my team relies on me, so I try to just push through it. 

But... sometimes, I'll be looking at, like, a basic drainage calculation, or a spreadsheet I've used for years, and... my mind just kind of blanks? It's silly, really. I just sit there rereading the same numbers over and over, and I just can't seem to trust myself to make a decision. 

I know I shouldn't let it get to me, and I'm sure I just need to concentrate harder. I don't want you to think I'm doing a bad job at work or anything—I always get things done eventually! It just takes me a little longer right now. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound like I can't do my job at all.
Outside of your work responsibilities, have you noticed that you no longer find pleasure or interest in the hobbies or activities that you used to enjoy?

Um... well, I guess I haven't been doing as much outside of work lately. But I think that's mostly just because I've been so tired, you know? 

I usually love hiking and, um, I used to go to this pottery class on weekends. But recently, I just... I haven't really felt up to it. I'll tell myself I'm going to go, and then I just end up staying home. I know I should force myself to get out more, and I'm really trying to be better about it. I just don't want to be lazy.

I mean, it's not like I hate those things now! I'm sure I'll get back into them once things settle down and I catch up on some sleep. It's totally normal to need a break from hobbies sometimes, right? I hope it doesn't sound like I've just given up on everything. I really am trying to keep a good attitude about it all.
Are there times during the day when you feel like you can briefly 'snap out of it' or feel a temporary lift in your mood if something good happens or if you are distracted by something pleasant?

Um... I guess sometimes? Like, if someone at the office brings in donuts or if a coworker tells a funny story, I'll smile and maybe feel a little lighter for a minute. I really try to appreciate those little moments, you know? 

But... to be honest, it doesn't usually last very long. Even if I laugh at a joke, as soon as I turn back to my desk, it's like... that heavy feeling just settles right back over me. I know I should try harder to hold onto the good feelings. I don't want to be a downer for the people around me, so I try to act like I'm doing okay when we're chatting. 

I hope that makes sense? I mean, I can still smile and everything, I'm not totally miserable all the time! I just... I guess the good moments don't really stick around the way they used to. Is that what you meant by snapping out of it?
Beyond the difficulty with your hobbies, have you felt a persistent sense of physical exhaustion or a significant lack of energy throughout most of your day?

Um... well, I guess I have been feeling pretty tired lately. But I really try not to let it slow me down too much! I mean, I know everyone gets tired, especially with work and everything. 

But... if I'm being completely honest, it does feel a bit heavier than just needing a good night's sleep. It's almost like... getting through a normal workday feels like I'm dragging wet concrete around with me. And sometimes, even just doing little things, like taking a shower or opening my laptop in the morning... it just takes so much more energy than I seem to have right now. 

I know I shouldn't complain, and I'm really trying to push through it. I don't want to sound lazy or like I'm just making excuses! I always make sure I get my work done, I promise. It's just... taking a lot out of me lately. Does that... does that sound like normal tiredness to you? I hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing.
Beyond the fatigue and trouble concentrating, have you been feeling a sense of worthlessness or excessive guilt about the situation you're in?

Um... well, I really try not to think like that. I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself, and I'm really trying to stay positive! I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself all day. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... sometimes my mind just sort of spirals. I'll start thinking that I'm just a terrible engineer, or... or a failed wife, and that I'm just this huge burden on everyone around me. I know it's silly to think that way, and I try to snap out of it! But I end up replaying every little mistake... like a missed calculation at work, or an email where I sounded a bit too tense... and it just feels like proof that I ruin everything I touch. 

I know I'm probably overreacting, and I really am trying to be better about not beating myself up so much. I don't want to sound like I'm whining or anything! I know I need to just work harder and fix my attitude. Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound completely awful for thinking those things.
Have you noticed that you are moving or speaking much more slowly than usual, or conversely, that you feel so restless that you have trouble sitting still?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I don't think so? I always try to keep up a good pace at work and be responsive when people talk to me. I don't want anyone to think I'm slacking off or ignoring them! 

I guess I might be a tiny bit slower getting started in the morning, just because I'm so tired, like I mentioned before. But once I'm up and moving, I think I'm pretty much my normal self. And I definitely haven't been pacing around or feeling super restless or anything like that. I usually just sit at my desk and try to focus on my projects. 

So, yeah, I think I'm moving and talking fine! I hope I'm answering that right? I just haven't really noticed any big changes like that.

When you look back at these feelings of worthlessness, the difficulty concentrating, the loss of interest in hobbies, and the fatigue, do you feel like these are things that only started because of the stress of your divorce, or do you feel like you have experienced these same symptoms to this degree at other times in your life, even when things were going well?

Um... well, I think I've always been a pretty upbeat person, mostly! I really try to be resilient, you know? I don't want you to think I'm just someone who is always down or complaining. 

But... I guess if I really think about it, this heavy feeling... it's really just been the last month or so. It all sort of started around the time the financial stuff with the divorce got really messy. I mean, it's normal to feel a little overwhelmed when you're dealing with lawyers and splitting up accounts, right? I just keep telling myself it's just the stress of the situation and that I'll bounce back soon! 

I really haven't felt this... this bad... at other times in my life, especially not when things were going well. I usually handle stress a lot better than this, I promise! It's just... this past month has just been a lot, and this feeling has just been hanging over me since that financial mess started. Does that make sense? I hope that's a normal reaction to all of this.
